title: Opposition boycotts IEBC meeting, gives commission until December and threatens protests from January
key_points: Opposition leaders stayed away from an IEBC meeting with political parties on Wednesday, November 25.
They say the IEBC has until December to act on their demands, or they will lead protests from January.
The meeting went ahead. Other party leaders criticised Gachagua's 'briefcase parties' remark.
Separately, the IEBC said it has not cleared Gachagua to run for president in 2027.
content:
Kenya's main opposition leaders boycotted a meeting called by the electoral commission (IEBC) on Wednesday, November 25. They said they will lead countrywide protests from January if the commission does not meet their demands by December.

Instead of attending, the leaders held a joint press briefing in Nairobi. The IEBC meeting went ahead with other political parties.

Who was there

The Star and Mwakilishi report that the briefing brought together former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua (DCP leader), former Chief Justice David Maraga (United Green Movement), former Attorney General Justin Muturi (Democratic Party), Martha Karua (People's Liberation Party), Fred Matiang'i (Jubilee), Jimmy Wanjigi (Safina) and Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro.

According to Citizen Digital, this was the second time the opposition has stayed away from IEBC talks. On November 19 some of them walked out of an earlier meeting.

Why they stayed away

Gachagua said the meeting was organised by the State Department for Interior, not the IEBC alone, and asked why President William Ruto was speaking for the commission. He called the parties that attended "briefcase parties". "We are not willing to engage in a charade," he said, according to Citizen Digital.

Maraga said attending would only approve decisions that were already made. He said the IEBC is "captured", a claim the commission has not accepted.

What they want

The Star reports that the opposition's demands include:

  • an independent audit of the voter register to remove dead and double-registered voters;
  • open election technology that can be checked independently;
  • results sent electronically from polling stations and shown live, with a public results website;
  • scrapping the National Tallying Centre;
  • hiring returning officers on merit.

The Star says the IEBC has until December to respond. If it does not, the leaders say they will mobilise Kenyans from January to take their complaints to IEBC offices across the country. Kenyans.co.ke reported Gachagua's timeline a little differently, saying action could start "next month". Kenyans.co.ke also reported that Maraga called for voter registration desks in US states with many Kenyans.

The other side

Citizen Digital reports that the IEBC briefed the parties that attended on voter registration, the voter register audit and buying election technology. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the commission will follow court directions on the national tallying centre and treat all parties equally.

Leaders of parties that attended rejected Gachagua's words. Evans Misati, chair of the Political Parties Liaison Committee, said DCP is one of 105 registered parties and will get no special treatment. Ford Kenya chairman Joel Ruhu said: "We are political parties just like the rest."

President Ruto has warned politicians against threatening the IEBC or organising protests against it, according to The Star and Citizen Digital.

IEBC: Gachagua not yet cleared

Also on Wednesday, the IEBC said it "has neither cleared nor made any determination" on whether Gachagua can run for president. This came after its legal director, Chrispine Owiye, told journalists on Tuesday that leaders whose removal is under appeal are not automatically barred.

The commission said a presidential candidate's eligibility will be decided at the nomination stage, which has not started. Gachagua was impeached in October 2024. The High Court upheld his removal in June 2026, and his appeal is still pending. No response from Gachagua to the IEBC statement had been reported.

Kenya's next general election is due in August 2027.
